LolF binds lipidated cargo, recruits LolA and couples conformational changes driven by the LolD ATPase to cargo release from the inner membrane.

A5FI22.description: Fjoh_2111 (LolA1) is a LolA-family lipoprotein-trafficking protein of Flavobacterium johnsoniae UW101, predicted to act as a soluble periplasmic carrier. It supports delivery of a subset of lipoproteins to the outer membrane, including components needed for gliding motility and type IX secretion. Native loss of LolA1 reduces the outer-membrane abundance of GldJ and GldK and disrupts these downstream systems. Other lipoproteins retain localization without the known LolA/LolB proteins, indicating alternative trafficking routes. LolA1 has distinct functional requirements from its pigment-locus paralog LolA2 and is not freely exchangeable with the E. coli carrier under the tested conditions.

core_functions.description: Inferred periplasmic carriage of lipoproteins supporting their delivery to the outer membrane. The specific LolA architecture and native UW101 client-localization phenotypes support this role; purified target transfer and direct target compartment fractionation have not been demonstrated in the consulted study.

A5FL25.description: Fjoh_1066 encodes LolB1, a structurally divergent LolB-like lipoprotein in Flavobacterium johnsoniae UW101. Native deletion and complementation implicate it in delivery of a subset of lipoproteins to the outer membrane, including clients needed for gliding and type IX secretion. Its predicted LolB fold, lipoprotein signal and functional loop support an inferred outer-membrane insertion role. These studies establish cellular trafficking function rather than a purified-protein insertion reaction. Other paralogs and retained lipoprotein localization in strains lacking known LolA/LolB proteins show that LolB1 is neither universally essential nor the only delivery route.

core_functions.description: Inferred promotion of lipid-anchor insertion for a subset of outer-membrane lipoprotein clients, supported by native trafficking phenotypes and LolB-like structural/functional evidence.

P0ADC3.description: LolC is a four-pass inner-membrane subunit of the Escherichia coli LolCDE lipoprotein-release complex. Together with LolE, it forms the pockets that bind the lipid anchor of mature outer-membrane-destined lipoproteins. The Hook and Pad surfaces in its large periplasmic domain recruit LolA and prepare the carrier to receive cargo. Two cytoplasmic LolD ATPase subunits drive the conformational cycle that extracts lipoproteins from the periplasmic leaflet of the inner membrane. This releases already translocated cargo into the periplasm rather than moving it through the inner-membrane bilayer.

core_functions.description: Contribution to the LolCDE recognition-and-release activity through joint lipid-anchor binding and recruitment of the LolA carrier by the periplasmic Hook and Pad surfaces.

P61316.description: LolA is the soluble periplasmic carrier that transfers mature outer-membrane lipoproteins between LolCDE in the inner membrane and LolB at the outer membrane of Escherichia coli. Recruitment by the periplasmic domain of LolC enables cargo loading into LolA's hydrophobic cavity, which shields the lipid anchor during passage through the aqueous periplasm. LolA then delivers cargo to LolB for membrane insertion. LolCDE normally excludes inner-membrane retention substrates at the extraction step. LolA is essential in ordinary E. coli backgrounds, although conditional bypass of LolA and LolB is possible when lipoprotein toxicity and envelope stress responses are altered.

core_functions.description: Periplasmic carriage of mature outer-membrane-destined lipoproteins from the LolCDE release complex to the outer-membrane receptor LolB, binding the lipid anchor in a hydrophobic cavity.

P61320.description: LolB is a lipid-anchored outer-membrane lipoprotein of Escherichia coli whose periplasm-facing domain accepts mature lipoproteins from LolA and promotes insertion of their lipid anchors into the outer membrane. It is the terminal acceptor and insertion component of the canonical Lol trafficking pathway. LolB is essential in ordinary E. coli backgrounds; this requirement can be bypassed under altered lipoprotein-toxicity and envelope-stress conditions. Its historical HemM name does not reflect its established lipoprotein-trafficking function.

P75957.description: LolD is the cytoplasmic ATP-binding and ATP-hydrolyzing subunit of the Escherichia coli LolCDE lipoprotein-release complex. Two LolD copies associate with the inner-membrane subunits LolC and LolE, coupling the nucleotide cycle to extraction of mature lipoproteins from the periplasmic leaflet and transfer to LolA. ATP binding drives conformational rearrangements in the cargo-binding assembly; ATP hydrolysis is required for sustained membrane release and resets the cycle in structural models. LolD powers extracytoplasmic cargo extraction rather than transport of cargo through the inner-membrane bilayer.

P75958.description: LolE is a four-pass inner-membrane subunit of the Escherichia coli LolCDE lipoprotein-release complex. LolE and LolC jointly form lipid-anchor-binding pockets, while a cleft on the LolE periplasmic domain contacts a short segment of the cargo polypeptide and promotes efficient release. Two LolD ATPase subunits drive the conformational cycle, and LolC recruits the LolA carrier. LolD and LolE can support release in a particular in vitro reconstitution, whereas the canonical cellular machinery requires both LolC and LolE. Cargo is extracted from the periplasmic leaflet, not translocated through the inner-membrane bilayer.

Q9A261.description: CC_3705 encodes the LolA-family periplasmic lipoprotein carrier of Caulobacter vibrioides CB15. Its fold and heterologous complementation support carriage of mature lipoproteins toward the outer membrane. A CB15-derived protein with an E. coli-compatible C terminus also substitutes for LolB in a permissive E. coli host, and separation-of-function experiments implicate the retained Caulobacter loop in insertion. These results support an inferred bifunctional carrier/insertion role for native CC_3705; they do not directly measure lipoprotein delivery or insertion by unmodified CC_3705 in Caulobacter.
